title: A leader who spends a mandate for change on preserving the existing system keeps the structures the mandate was meant to replace
body:
- A mandate of this kind carries the political capital needed to redesign broken institutions only because voters granted it unusually broad authority, not because the capital itself is ordinary.
- Spending that capital on stabilizing the system preserves the broken structures the mandate existed to overhaul.
- Stabilization preserves continuity and legitimacy while leaving the deeper dysfunction intact.
- Case: Obama's 2008 election with unified Democratic control of Congress.
conversion: A mandate granted to replace the existing structures instead produces their preservation.
